description: Implement a mixed-precision blocked Cholesky whose trailing updates use Blackwell tensor-core operations while diagonal panels and correction-sensitive steps remain FP32, targeting compute throughput without relaxing the reconstruction contract.

Dispatch n>=4096 to a 1024-column right-looking blocked Cholesky: FP32 cuSOLVER diagonal panels and triangular solves with TF32 tensor-core batched trailing updates; all validation and benchmark checks passed.

Lower the mixed-precision dispatch threshold to n=2048 so the 1024-column blocked TF32 update covers both n=2048 benchmark batches; validation passed, while added panel/solve overhead raised the full geomean.
Restore n>=4096 dispatch and widen FP32 panels/TF32 update tiles from 1024 to 2048; single-matrix n=4096..32768 timings fell, while batched n=4096 rose, producing a 1861.686 us geomean.

Adapt panel width by batch: 2048 for single matrices and 1024 for batched inputs, preserving the faster single-matrix updates while avoiding the batched 2048-panel slowdown; all checks passed at 1839.054 us.

Widen the single-matrix FP32 panel to 4096 while retaining 1024 for batches; fewer factor/solve/update stages reduced the n=4096, 8192, 16384, and 32768 times to 1664.597, 5142.118, 17922.752, and 74462.988 us, with 1783.854 us overall.

Widen the single-matrix panel to 8192; correctness passed, and this run measured 3104.626 us overall. Unchanged sub-4096 baseline-dispatch shapes also rose by roughly 1.6x in this Modal sample, alongside the wider-panel large-shape timings.

Replace full baddbmm trailing updates with a cuBLAS TF32 SYRK that computes only row-major lower triangles; extension compilation reached link but failed because the CUDA wheel exposes no lib64/libcublas.so for -lcublas.

Link the cuBLAS extension against the discovered CUDA runtime and run scalar TF32 Ssyrk per batch, updating only the required lower triangle. All checks passed; n>=8192 SYRK timings rose versus tensor-core baddbmm, yielding 2051.866 us overall.

Replace scalar SYRK with one explicit cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx rank-k update using CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F_FAST_TF32; full tensor-core updates restored large-shape performance and measured 1787.023 us overall.
Feed the compact solve_triangular result directly to explicit TF32 GEMM instead of the gapped in-output panel view; large-shape timings were similar, while this full sample measured 1817.429 us.

Quantize only solved trailing panels to BF16, accumulate their explicit cuBLAS rank-k updates in FP32, and keep diagonal factors/solves/output FP32. Every benchmark reconstruction passed; n=8192,16384,32768 fell to 5074.797,16512.277,62339.616 us and the geomean reached 1745.790 us.

Use FP16 rather than BF16 panel operands for Blackwell tensor-core trailing updates, retaining FP32 accumulation, panels, solves, and output. All reconstructions passed; batched n=4096 reached 6245.229 us and the full geomean reached 1732.619 us.

Widen the batched FP32 panel/FP16 update tile from 1024 to 2048 while retaining 4096 for single matrices; correctness passed, but batched n=4096 measured 9396.760 us and the full geomean was 1826.777 us.
Narrow batched panels to 512 while keeping single-matrix panels at 4096; additional FP16 tensor-core updates reduced batched n=4096 to 5906.963 us, with all checks passing and 1724.869 us overall.

Narrow batched panels again to 256, shifting more rank-k work to FP16 tensor cores; batched n=4096 measured 5648.637 us and the all-shape geomean reached 1718.550 us with every reconstruction passing.
Narrow batched FP32 panels to 128 and continue FP16 tensor-core trailing updates; batched n=4096 fell to 5399.046 us and all 15 benchmark shapes passed at 1714.240 us geomean.
Narrow batched panels to 64, increasing FP16 update stages; correctness passed, while batched n=4096 measured 7725.602 us in this sample and the all-shape geomean was 1796.057 us.

Restore 128-wide batched panels and extend the mixed FP16-update path from n>=4096 to n>=2048; both n=2048 shapes passed reconstruction at 2391.587 and 4742.528 us, reducing the full geomean to 1675.654 us.

Remove the persistent torch allow_tf32 mutation so later input generation and unrelated calls retain their original precision state. All checks passed; this sample measured 1804.240 us, with FP32 panel/solve work notably higher on the large single-matrix shapes.

Scope torch's fast FP32 library policy to the blocked factorization with try/finally restoration, preserving fast panel/solve dispatch without changing later harness input generation or checks. Validation residuals returned to baseline patterns; the benchmark passed at 1692.258 us.

Dispatch high-batch n=1024 (batch>=16) through the 128-panel FP16-update schedule while retaining cuSOLVER for low-batch 1024. The batch-60 shape fell from roughly 2.9 ms to 2468.568 us, all checks passed, and geomean reached 1659.929 us.

Extend the 128-panel FP16-update dispatch to high-batch n=512 (batch>=64). Correctness passed, but batch-640 n=512 measured 4004.250 us versus roughly 3.78 ms on cuSOLVER, producing 1680.195 us overall.

Use 256-wide panels specifically for high-batch n=512 while retaining 128 elsewhere. The n=512 batch-640 shape measured 4158.970 us, while this full Modal sample measured 1656.676 us overall with all checks passing.

Return n=512 to cuSOLVER and use 256-wide panels for high-batch n=1024, retaining 128 at n>=2048. The n=1024 batch-60 shape measured 2446.749 us; all checks passed and the full sample measured 1672.704 us.
Use 256-wide FP32 panels for both n=1024 and n=2048 mixed paths, retaining 128 above. The two n=2048 shapes measured 2635.461 and 5119.776 us in this sample; all checks passed at 1689.908 us overall.

Add a dtype-generic cuBLAS update: use fast-TF32 FP32 panels for high-batch n=512 and FP16 panels above it, while restoring 128-wide n=2048 panels. Reconstruction passed, but n=512 batch-640 measured 4142.022 us and the full metric was 1684.193 us.
Remove unprofitable n=512 and generic-TF32 paths; keep FP16 tensor-core trailing updates for n>=2048 and high-batch n=1024 with tuned panel widths

Best candidate c5f12bb measured 1647.471 us versus the 2153.690 us baseline (23.5% lower latency, about 1.31x speedup) and passed build plus all 17 validation cases and the input-variation guard. It uses FP32 diagonal panels and triangular solves, converts only solved panels to FP16, and performs FP32-accumulating cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx trailing updates on Blackwell tensor cores; dispatch is limited to profitable n>=2048 shapes and batch>=16 at n=1024, with scoped TF32 state restoration. Panel tuning selected 4096 for single matrices, 256 for n=1024 high-batch, and 128 for larger batched matrices. Measured alternatives showed BF16, SYRK, compact solved buffers, n=512 mixed/TF32 paths, and other tested panel sizes slower. Concrete follow-ups are combining this large-shape path with other workers' small/mid-size wins, trying 96/160/192 batched panel widths, using cublasLt or CUTLASS to fuse/avoid FP16 conversion, and exploring triangular-only tensor-core rank-k scheduling.
